title: A Kitchen for the Summer
premise: Ulyana Vane has spent ten years rebuilding her life around her daughter, her bookshop, and a careful silence about the summer that ended everything. When the town's last orchard is left to both her and Daniel Reyes — the man she once loved, who testified against her brother to save his own family — they are legally bound to co-manage it until the harvest festival or lose it to a developer. Forced into shared labor among dying apple trees, old testimony and new evidence collide: Ulyana discovers Daniel took the fall for someone else entirely, while he learns what her silence cost her. At the festival's closing night, one of them must finally say the rehearsed sentence — 'I should have chosen you' — before the deed, and their second chance, expires.
about_author: Vesper Marchetti is a former small-town bookseller who writes romances about people whose timing is always slightly wrong. She lives near an orchard she refuses to name, where she does her best thinking between harvests.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A lawyer's letter reveals the orchard was willed jointly to Ulyana and Daniel Reyes, her first love and the man whose testimony helped convict her brother. She wants to refuse; the will's terms forbid it until the festival. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in disbelief, the past arriving with legal force.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Rehearsed Sentences
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He returns to town carrying guilt he's never confessed: his testimony was coerced, naming Ulyana's brother to protect his own father. Seeing Ulyana across the orchard gate, he can't say any of it. Emotional beat: cowardice disguised as composure, cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. They negotiate rules: no talk of the trial, split hours, no unsupervised contact with Ulyana's daughter, Wren. The developer's agent circles, offering buyouts. Emotional beat: brittle professionalism over live wires; each rule a wall they both keep testing.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Clearing storm damage, they find initials carved in the oldest apple tree — theirs, from the summer before everything broke. Wren wanders in and charms Daniel before Ulyana can intervene. Emotional beat: tenderness ambushing them both; grief for the people they were.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Digging through his father's old papers for the deed abstract, Daniel finds a letter proving his father orchestrated the coercion — and that a third person committed the crime. He pockets it instead of telling Ulyana. Emotional beat: the price of survival compounding interest; shame choosing silence again.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A late frost threatens the crop; they work through the night with smudge pots and borrowed blankets, and almost-touches become real ones. The developer escalates, pressuring the town council. Emotional beat: warmth earned through shared labor, immediately shadowed by the secret Daniel is keeping.

chapters.title: Wren Asks About the Orchard Man
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, intimate scale. Wren, eight and unguarded, asks why Daniel looks at her mother 'like the sad endings in books.' Ulyana realizes she's falling again and panics — duty to her daughter, her brother's memory, her hard-won stability all say stop. Emotional beat: love against duty, argued alone at midnight.

chapters.title: The Letter Comes Out Wrong
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV turning dual. Ulyana finds the hidden letter during inventory; Daniel confesses the coercion but not yet the third party's identity — it's the town's beloved retired judge, the festival's founder. Ulyana feels betrayed by the half-truth and walks out. Emotional beat: climax of mistrust; justice outside the law suddenly demands courage neither has budgeted for.

chapters.title: Closing Night at the Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, rapid cuts. Festival deadline arrives; the developer waits with paperwork. Daniel takes the stage during the judging ceremony and names the judge publicly, surrendering his family's safety for the truth. Ulyana, watching, understands the sentence he's been unable to say. Emotional beat: public reckoning, private terror, the crowd as witness.

chapters.title: A Kitchen for the Summer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Weeks later: the judge under investigation, her brother's conviction reopened, the orchard saved as a community trust. In the orchard's converted packing shed — now a kitchen — Daniel finally says the rehearsed sentence, and Ulyana answers with her own version. Wren sets a third plate without being asked. Emotional beat: resolution as quiet domesticity; second chances arriving exactly on time after all.
